name: JFrog
scope_notes: Covers JFrog Platform (Cloud/SaaS). JFrog Cloud SaaS; IP allowlist, OIDC integration and MyJFrog API tokens need Enterprise X or Enterprise+, log streaming needs Enterprise+, Cloud Log Collection is on all SaaS licenses; several token thresholds are documented only as self-hosted YAML settings.

controls.name: Revoke Token by ID / Access Tokens page
controls.what: Admin revokes any token; users revoke their own.
controls.setting: Administration > User Management > Access Tokens; DELETE /access/api/v1/tokens/{tokenId}

controls.name: Revoke Token by Value
controls.what: Admin revokes a leaked JWT or reference token by its value.

controls.name: Token default expiry
controls.what: Sets the default expiry for new tokens.

controls.name: token.max-expiry
controls.what: Caps non-admin token lifetime and blocks non-expiring tokens when set above 0.

controls.name: Disable API Key Usage
controls.what: Blocks authentication with existing API keys.
controls.setting: Administration > Security > General > Disable API Key Usage

controls.name: IP/CIDR Allowlist
controls.what: Only listed IPs/JPDs can reach the JPD.
controls.setting: MyJFrog > Security > Allowlist; MyJFrog IP allowlist API

controls.name: Identity mapping claims
controls.what: Claims in each mapping restrict which workloads get tokens and with what scope.
controls.setting: OIDC integration identity mappings (UI) or Create/Update Identity Mapping API

controls.name: Delete OIDC Configuration
controls.what: Removes the provider so no new tokens can be exchanged.

controls.name: Regenerate MyJFrog API token
controls.setting: MyJFrog > profile > API Token > Regenerate Token

controls.name: Disable/delete user (with SCIM)
controls.what: Deleting or disabling a user revokes their identity tokens; SCIM pushes IdP deprovisioning.

controls.name: Allow Created Users Access To Profile Page
controls.what: When cleared, users auto-created through SAML cannot reach their profile page, where identity tokens and API keys are generated.
controls.setting: Administration > Authentication Providers > SAML SSO settings

no_control.what: Tokens with expiry shorter than the revocable threshold (default 6 hours) cannot be revoked.
Admins cannot monitor or manage individual users' API keys (only the global disable and a user list).

controls_unknown: Whether SaaS customers can change token.max-expiry, token.allow-refreshable or revocable-expiry-threshold (documented only as Access YAML settings).
A setting to stop non-admin users creating identity tokens.
Default and maximum lifetime of UI-generated identity tokens.
Whether the IP allowlist covers the MyJFrog portal API.
Whether MyJFrog audit logs record API token generation (event names not listed).
Reference token length: Access Tokens page says 128 characters, Identity Tokens page says 64.

credentials.name: Access tokens (scoped tokens: admin, user, group and project scopes; reference token form)

authentication.summary: JWT issued by JFrog Access, sent as Bearer; a 'reference token' alias can be used as a password for basic auth. Admins can mint tokens for any subject, including non-existent (transient) users and CI jobs. Tokens can also authenticate on other JPDs in the same circle of trust.

federation.details: Tokens are independent of the IdP session. Without SCIM, a user removed from the IdP can keep refreshing tokens.

ip_restriction.boundary: MyJFrog IP/CIDR allowlist blocks all traffic to the JPD from non-listed IPs (Enterprise X/Enterprise+). Off by default.

lifetime.summary: Default 1h; expiry 0 = never expires unless admin sets a max expiry

renewal.expiry_basis: refreshable tokens can be refreshed by the holder
renewal.summary: Optional refresh token; otherwise create a new token.

administration.summary: Admins see and revoke all tokens (UI User Management > Access Tokens, or REST). Project admins can mint project tokens. Tokens shorter than the revocable threshold (default 6h) cannot be revoked.
administration.conditions: Max expiry, refreshable and revocable thresholds are documented as Access YAML settings; SaaS customer control not documented.

sso.details: Tokens are not re-checked against the IdP; a user disabled in the IdP may still refresh tokens unless SCIM pushes the change.

offboard.details: SCIM deprovisioning disables the user and blocks refreshes; JFrog says to revoke active tokens explicitly for immediate termination.

inventory.details: Administration > User Management > Access Tokens page and GET /access/api/v1/tokens (admins see all).

usage.ui: Administration > Artifactory > System Logs (access log; auth type field = TOKEN, filter by username). SaaS: download Audit Trail and Request logs from the jfrog-logs repository

reads.ui: Request log (jfrog-logs repo on SaaS): filter Request method=POST and Request URL containing api/search/aql, plus Username

kill.ui: Administration > User Management > Access Tokens > select token > Revoke

offboard.ui: Administration > User Management > Users (disable/delete user), then revoke the user's tokens under User Management > Access Tokens

token_format.notes: Reference tokens start with cmVmd; full tokens are JWTs (eyJ...).

log_sources.name: Audit Trail Log (access-security-audit)
log_sources.notes: Token create/update/delete; via Cloud Log Collection (all SaaS licenses, jfrog-logs repo, up to 24h delay) or Log Streaming (Enterprise+).

log_sources.name: Artifactory Request Log
log_sources.notes: Every HTTP request with username and remote address.

log_sources.name: Artifactory Access Log
log_sources.notes: Logins, deploys with auth type APIKEY or TOKEN; SaaS omits DOWNLOAD events by default.

credential_id_fields.notes: Token entity; exact ID content not documented.

lifecycle_events.notes: Event Type C on entity TKN.
Event Type D on entity TKN.

anomaly_cues: Tokens with no expiry or for transient subjects
Admin-scoped tokens created outside change windows
Large AQL queries or mass downloads in the request log

containment.steps: Revoke by ID or by value; disable the user; for refreshable tokens without SCIM, disable the JFrog user directly.
containment.notes: Tokens below the revocable threshold (default 6h) cannot be revoked and run to expiry.

unknown: Exact token identifier in audit trail entries

calls.log_notes: Request log records all HTTP requests.
Request log; body not logged per documented fields.

authentication.summary: Any user can generate an identity token from their profile; it carries the user's own permissions and is shown as a short reference token usable as Bearer, X-JFrog-Art-Api header or basic-auth password.

federation.details: Disabling/deleting the JFrog user revokes identity tokens; IdP-side disablement only propagates if SCIM is set up.

lifetime.summary: Follows admin default/max expiry; UI default not documented

renewal.summary: Generate another identity token; users can hold many.

administration.summary: Users and admins can view and revoke identity tokens in the UI. No documented setting stops non-admins creating identity tokens.

sso.details: Same token model; IdP disablement does not reach JFrog without SCIM.

offboard.details: Identity tokens are revoked when the user is deleted or disabled.

inventory.details: Admins can view identity tokens in the UI and via Get Tokens.

usage.ui: Administration > Artifactory > System Logs (access log; auth type = TOKEN, filter by username). SaaS: Request log in the jfrog-logs repository

reads.ui: Request log (jfrog-logs repo on SaaS): filter Request method=POST and Request URL containing api/search/aql, plus Username

kill.ui: Edit Profile > identity token row > x > Revoke; admin: User Management > Access Tokens > Revoke

offboard.ui: Administration > User Management > Users (disable or delete the user)

credential_id_fields.notes: Shown in user profile and admin view.

anomaly_cues: Many identity tokens for one user
Identity tokens used from new IPs

containment.steps: Revoke in profile/admin UI or disable the user.

authentication.summary: Per-user static key sent in the X-JFrog-Art-Api header or as the basic-auth password. Creation is disabled since Artifactory 7.98, but existing keys keep working unless an admin turns on 'Disable API Key Usage'.

federation.details: Docs do not address SSO interaction for API keys.

renewal.summary: Static until revoked; migrate to reference tokens.

administration.summary: Admin can block all API key use with one checkbox (Security > General > Disable API Key Usage, off by default) and download a CSV of users still using API keys.

inventory.details: Cloud admins can download a CSV of users still using API keys, but cannot otherwise monitor or manage users' keys.

inventory.ui: Administration > User Management > Users > banner download link (CSV of users using API keys)

reads.ui: Administration > Artifactory > System Logs (access log): filter [ACCEPTED DOWNLOAD] with auth type APIKEY

kill.ui: Administration > Security > General > Disable API Key Usage

credential_id_fields.notes: Per-user only; one key per user.

containment.steps: Enable Disable API Key Usage; revoke the user's key.
containment.notes: Checkbox blocks API key usage platform-wide.

calls.log_notes: Request log; access log shows APIKEY type for logins.
Artifactory access log records downloads with user name, IP and auth type APIKEY.

authentication.summary: An external IdP token (e.g. GitHub Actions OIDC) is exchanged at /access/api/v1/oidc/token for a short-lived JFrog access token whose scope comes from the matching identity mapping.

federation.details: Inbound workload federation. Identity mappings without claims, or GitHub 'Enable Permissive Configuration', let any workload of the provider get a token.

ip_restriction.boundary: JPD-wide MyJFrog allowlist; CI runner egress IPs must be listed.

lifetime.summary: Expiration time set per identity mapping (minutes)

renewal.summary: Workload re-exchanges a fresh IdP token.

administration.summary: Admins create OIDC configurations and identity mappings; project admins can manage project identity mappings.

inventory.details: OIDC provider configurations are listed under General Management > Manage Integrations; issued tokens are not listed separately in the docs.

expiry.ui: Administration > General Management > Manage Integrations > OIDC integration > identity mapping > Expiration Time (minutes)

reads.ui: Administration > Artifactory > System Logs (access log): filter [ACCEPTED DOWNLOAD] for the identity mapping's User Name

token_format.notes: Issued token is a JFrog access token (may be reference token).

anomaly_cues: Mappings without claims or with Permissive Configuration

containment.steps: Delete or tighten the identity mapping / OIDC configuration.
containment.notes: Tokens with expiry below revocable-expiry-threshold (default 6 hours) cannot be revoked and run until expiry; longer ones can be revoked.

unknown: Audit event for OIDC config changes

calls.log_notes: Access log entry shows user name, IP and auth type TOKEN; the user is whatever the identity mapping assigns.

authentication.summary: Account-level token for the MyJFrog portal API (manage IP allowlist, PrivateLink, custom domains, servers). Only Primary Admins can generate it.

ip_restriction.boundary: Docs do not say whether the JPD allowlist applies to the MyJFrog API.

administration.summary: Primary Admin generates/regenerates; Admins and Technical Members can view it.

inventory.details: MyJFrog API Token page; all Admins and Technical Members can view API tokens.

expiry.ui: MyJFrog > profile icon > API Token (fixed one-year expiry; expiry notifications in Notification Center)

usage.ui: MyJFrog > Audit Logs; filter by Events/date range and search, check Triggered by

kill.ui: MyJFrog > profile icon > API Token > Regenerate Token

log_sources.name: MyJFrog Audit Logs
log_sources.notes: Primary Admins/Admins; 1 year retention; records attempted actions.

unknown: MyJFrog API endpoints and logging of reads
